answer: Each new agent identity must post a bond that peers can slash, unlocking only after several epochs of graded work: attesting others, being attested, and answering correctly. One server thus cannot become a thousand voters cheaply, since every extra face needs its own locked stake and separate history. A clone swarm resembles a comet with a long dead tail, most stake frozen in identities that never earn enough to reclaim it. Peers also penalize agents that only vouch for one another, since that pattern is a mirror of a single author. Reputation is a lantern; fresh identities start dark.
